clue.text: Extinguishes the candle and passes on

definitions.meaning: to put out a flame by pinching or capping the wick

explanation.surface: Someone puts out a candle and leaves the room, or perhaps dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: one for putting out a wick, the other a slangy euphemism for dying.

clue.text: Angry outbursts in play

definitions.meaning: public tantrums or rows, as in 'don't make a fuss'
the subdivisions of an act in drama

explanation.definitionFit: A public display of temper is a fuss of this kind, and a drama is divided into these sections.

clue.text: Slovenly in duty — removed

indicators.note: the letters are moved away from their places into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sloppy on the job who gets dismissed from their post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges IN DUTY, read as re-moved, moved again.
explanation.definitionFit: Messy and disordered in habit or appearance, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Go effortlessly by bicycle to coast

definitions.meaning: to move along without effort or power

explanation.surface: Cycling down to the seaside without having to pedal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coast' looks like the seaside, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a bike without pedalling, and more generally drifting along without effort, are the same verb.

clue.text: News the teacher would welcome in any form?

definitions.text: the teacher would welcome in any form?
definitions.meaning: cleverness in pupils, in any class (form) of the school

explanation.surface: A teacher would be happy to hear news in any shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is a British school class, so a teacher welcomes brainy pupils in any class.
explanation.definitionFit: Military and spy information is called this, and so is mental ability, prized by teachers.

clue.text: Defect in hose used by firemen

definitions.meaning: a run in stockings or tights
the climbing frame of rungs on a fire engine

explanation.surface: A flaw spotted in the hose the fire brigade uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a fire hose, but here it means stockings, where a run is a defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in stockings is called this, and firefighters climb the rung-built version to reach upper windows.

clue.text: Get into a row

parts.note: read as forming a straight line rather than starting a quarrel

explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts one to read a quarrel, but it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things or oneself in a straight line is the verb meant.

clue.text: Where people once spent time underground

definitions.text: Where people once spent time underground

parts.words: Where people once spent time underground
parts.note: spent time read as served a prison sentence, in old castle cellars

explanation.walkthrough: 'spent time' suggests mining or sheltering, but it means serving time in a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground cells in medieval castles held prisoners serving their time.

clue.text: Sees dirt, becomes repelled

indicators.note: the letters turn into, or become, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sees dirt and is put off by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' rearranges the letters of SEES DIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: To have fended off or withstood an attack is a past-tense synonym of repelled.

clue.text: Petition to take meals in the lobby

indicators.note: the eating is placed in the middle of the lobby word

parts.note: an entry is an entrance hall or lobby
to take meals is to eat

explanation.surface: A request to be allowed to eat in the hotel lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A petition is an earnest plea or request, which is a synonym.

clue.text: They play big parts in children's tales

definitions.text: They play big parts in children's tales

parts.words: They play big parts in children's tales
parts.note: big parts read literally: the enormous characters of fairy stories like Jack and the Beanstalk

explanation.surface: Actors who take the leading roles in children's stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big parts' sounds like major roles, but it means roles for huge characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres and huge beings such as the one atop the beanstalk are staple characters of fairy tales.

clue.text: The done things

parts.note: the 'done thing' is etiquette, but here simply things that have been done or accomplished

explanation.walkthrough: 'The done thing' is an idiom for good manners; here the phrase is read literally as completed deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplishments or feats are things successfully carried out.

clue.text: Provide money, enough to keep daughter

indicators.note: one word keeps, or holds, the other within it

parts.note: enow is an archaic word for enough

explanation.surface: Giving enough cash to support one's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: ENOW is an old poetic form of 'enough'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a lasting fund to an institution or person is to bestow money on it.

clue.text: Local managers

parts.note: the local is a pub, and those running pubs hold a licence to sell alcohol

explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' seems to mean regional, but in Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub, whose landlord must hold a licence to sell drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pub landlords hold a drinks licence, so those running the local are licence-holders.

clue.text: It may help in crime scene reconstruction

definitions.text: It may help in crime scene reconstruction

indicators.note: the letters are rebuilt into a new order, as a scene is rebuilt

explanation.surface: Something that might assist police reconstructing a crime scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstruction' rearranges the letters of IN CRIME SCENE; and a witness's memory of events may indeed help such a reconstruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Recollection of past events is what a witness offers when helping police rebuild what happened.

clue.text: Bird, fish and insect

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A list of creatures: a bird, a fish and a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: This scuttling household pest is a common insect.

clue.text: Collect items others consider useless

parts.note: describes picking through refuse for usable things

explanation.definitionFit: To search through discarded rubbish for anything usable, as foxes and gulls do.

clue.text: Witnesses appear to give it

parts.note: people summoned to court testify, which is what they provide

explanation.walkthrough: 'appear' suggests seeming, but witnesses appear in court in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony given in court is called this, the proof offered to a judge or jury.

clue.text: Polite assistance from bureaucrats?

parts.note: civil means courteous or polite
service is help or assistance given

explanation.surface: Asking whether officials ever give courteous help.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of government officials and administrators collectively; the question mark marks the plural-for-collective stretch.

clue.text: Ancient Greeks were riddled by it

definitions.text: Ancient Greeks were riddled by it

parts.words: Ancient Greeks were riddled by it
parts.note: the monster of Thebes posed a riddle to travellers and killed those who failed

explanation.walkthrough: 'riddled' suggests shot full of holes, but it means set riddles; Oedipus solved the one at Thebes.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged monster of Greek myth outside Thebes posed a famous riddle to passers-by.

clue.text: Elgar's variations of gamine

indicators.note: variations are altered versions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elgar composed a set of variations on a gamine theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variations of' rearranges GAMINE; the definition reads 'Elgar's ___ Variations', and the whole clue also names his famous work.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's best-known orchestral work is titled after this word for a puzzle or mystery.

clue.text: This guide wants you to go with him

definitions.text: This guide wants you to go with him

parts.words: This guide wants you to go with him
parts.note: the Latin name of the handbook means 'go with me', so it asks to be carried along

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Latin for 'go with me', the name for a handbook carried everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket handbook or manual kept constantly at hand is known by this Latin phrase.

clue.text: Effectively copes with sporting events

definitions.meaning: deals with successfully, as in satisfying a demand

explanation.definitionFit: One satisfies a challenge or demand this way, and athletic contests are also called this.

clue.text: Mature — or mature to a point

parts.note: ripe means fully mature, like fruit
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Growing up, or growing up to a certain degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to full development, as fruit does, is a synonym for maturing.

clue.text: Anne's going out with North Polar explorer

indicators.note: the letters leave their places and go out of order

explanation.surface: Anne is dating a man from the North who explores the poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' looks like dating, but it signals the letters of Anne's leaving their order; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Fridtjof Nansen was the Norwegian who crossed Greenland and pushed towards the North Pole.

clue.text: Requiring sound massage

indicators.note: the word for requiring is said aloud to give a word spoken the same

parts.note: requiring means needing

explanation.surface: In need of a good rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Working muscles with the hands, like dough, is a gerund synonym of massage.

clue.text: Nothing more than a 50-50 chance, nevertheless

indicators.note: the zero comes in addition to, on top of, the odds word

parts.note: evens are odds of one to one
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A chance no better than even, but still worth taking.
explanation.walkthrough: EVENS is the betting term for 50-50 odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning despite that or all the same, a synonym of nevertheless.

clue.text: It's a breathtaking experience

parts.note: breathtaking read literally: taking away one's breath, suffocation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathtaking' usually means stunning, but here it means literally stopping breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffocation from lack of oxygen literally stops a person breathing.
